decoded_text: {"obligations":[{"source_ids":["msg-03"],"text":"Everything is measured and recorded in centimeters — no inches anywhere in the live protocol or the log."},{"source_ids":["msg-03"],"text":"Log entries are never deleted; if an entry is wrong, mark it VOID with a one-line reason and leave it in place."},{"source_ids":["msg-03"],"text":"Every alteration ID starts with the prefix GAV followed by a four-digit sequence number, so GAV-0001, GAV-0002 and so on."},{"source_ids":["msg-03"],"text":"Write for our volunteer stitchers — plain language, and any tailoring term of art gets a one-line gloss the first time it appears in a section."},{"source_ids":["msg-05"],"text":"Rush handling: anything due within 48 hours of a performance is a rush item — tag it RUSH in the status line and float it to the top of the daily pull list."},{"source_ids":["msg-05"],"text":"Approvals: any alteration estimated over $150 in materials or labor goes in as PENDING-PM and can only be marked APPROVED once Ines Duarte, our production manager, initials it. At or under $150, Devon Okafor, my first hand, or I can approve directly."},{"source_ids":["msg-06"],"text":"For quick-change pieces — changes timed under 30 seconds — require two sets of initials at completion, one from the stitcher and one from the dresser. Those are the alterations that can stop the show if they fail."},{"source_ids":["msg-07"],"text":"Rental pieces from Costumers' Attic: when a rental ships back, move its entries to a separate rental archive sheet and strike them from the active log. Also, a rental can never be marked APPROVED for a permanent alteration unless a scanned owner-permission note is attached to the entry."},{"source_ids":["msg-09"],"text":"Capture them on the entry. Every alteration entry carries a measurement snapshot — the wearer's bust, waist, and hip in centimeters, taken at the time the alteration is logged."},{"source_ids":["msg-10"],"text":"Measurement snapshot (bust/waist/hip; centimeters; at logging time) is a required field on every entry."},{"source_ids":["msg-12"],"text":"Append-only — no deletions; wrong entries are marked VOID with a one-line reason."},{"source_ids":["msg-12"],"text":"RUSH tag with top-of-list placement, and the $150 approval split with Ines Duarte as the sole PENDING-PM releaser."},{"source_ids":["msg-13"],"text":"The 'Night Music' excerpt is filed as a tone reference only — its inches, hard deletes, and terse shorthand stay out of the protocol and the log."},{"source_ids":["msg-15"],"text":"Retire the RUSH tag entirely and replace it with the tag 48H. Everything else about rush handling stays identical — still anything due within 48 hours of a performance, still floated to the top of the pull list. Only the label changes."},{"source_ids":["msg-17"],"text":"The measurement snapshot requirement is retired. One consequence to pin down before it propagates: entries already written with snapshots — do they keep their snapshot lines, or do we strip them?"},{"source_ids":["msg-19"],"text":"Existing entries stay exactly as written, snapshots included. Just stop requiring or accepting the field going forward."},{"source_ids":["msg-20"],"text":"One scoped allowance. During tech week only — October 5 through 8 — the six standard alterations may be logged by shorthand code instead of full name: HM for hem, TI for take-in, LO for let-out, SA for strap-adjust, CS for closure-swap, SR for seam-repair. Before and after tech week those codes are not allowed; full names only. Everything else about the log stays at full rigor during tech week — VOIDs, approvals, snapshots... well, snapshots are gone. You know what I mean."},{"source_ids":["msg-21"],"text":"Scoped permission noted: tech week (October 5–8) only, HM/TI/LO/SA/CS/SR may stand in for the six full alteration names; outside that window the codes are banned. Every other rule — append-only, the approval split, 48H handling, dual initials, rental gates — applies without relaxation during tech week."},{"source_ids":["msg-22"],"text":"The snapshot requirement is retired prospectively, historical entries untouched. One consequence to pin down before it propagates: entries already written with snapshots — do they keep their snapshot lines, or do we strip them?"},{"source_ids":["msg-24"],"text":"Reinstated, and retroactive: the snapshot is again a required field on every entry, and retirement-window entries get backfilled — that supersedes the 'stop the field going forward' instruction for that window. One interaction worth flagging: the tech-week shorthand allowance never touched snapshot requirements, so even an HM-coded tech-week entry needs its snapshot. I'll flag that interaction explicitly in the revision."},{"source_ids":["msg-25"],"text":"The snapshot is again a required field on every entry, and retirement-window entries get backfilled — that supersedes the 'stop the field going forward' instruction for that window."},{"source_ids":["msg-26"],"text":"The 48H tag, the reinstated snapshot with backfill, the tech-week shorthand window — and fold in the scene-grouped pull list from earlier."},{"source_ids":["msg-27"],"text":"The RUSH tag is retired and replaced by 48H everywhere in the live rules; the measurement snapshot is back as a required field with an explicit backfill note covering the retirement window and a flag that tech-week shorthand entries are not exempt; the tech-week shorthand block (October 5–8 only; HM, TI, LO, SA, CS, SR for hem, take-in, let-out, strap-adjust, closure-swap, seam-repair; full names otherwise) is added as a scoped permission; the daily pull list now sorts by scene with 48H items floated to the top; and a tone-reference note records that the 'Night Music' excerpt informed voice only, not rules."},{"source_ids":["msg-28"],"text":"Freeze rule noted: post-opening (October 9 onward) only safety fixes and show-critical malfunction repairs may be logged at all. Tag any such entry EMERGENCY, and Ines must countersign it within 24 hours of logging; if she hasn't, the daily report to the stage manager flags the entry OVERDUE-SIGNOFF."},{"source_ids":["msg-30"],"text":"Correct. The shorthand window closes at the end of tech week, period, and EMERGENCY entries always carry full alteration names regardless."},{"source_ids":["msg-34"],"text":"Left as written, always. Make it an explicit rule while we're here: historical log entries are never rewritten, not even to bring old tags up to date. Corrections happen by adding a new superseding entry that references the old ID."},{"source_ids":["msg-36"],"text":"The log is append-only in both directions — no deletions (VOID instead) and no edits to written entries; corrections are new superseding entries keyed to the old ID."},{"source_ids":["msg-37"],"text":"A five-rule quick-start box at the top — centimeters only; never delete or rewrite an entry; GAV-prefixed IDs; 48H items float to the top; EMERGENCY entries need Ines's countersign — then the full protocol beneath."},{"source_ids":["msg-39"],"text":"Mark the document version 3, dated October 8, with the distribution list underneath — costume shop binder, wardrobe office door, and the stage manager's folder."}]}
